# Commit hooks exec a hard-coded per-user path → `git worktree add` and `wl sync` fail

## Problem statement

The committed hooks `.githooks/post-checkout`, `.githooks/post-merge` and
`.githooks/post-rewrite` unconditionally `exec` the absolute path
`/home/rgardler/.config/pi/.githooks/worklog-post-pull`. That path is
per-user and machine-specific, so on any host where it is absent (a different
username, a clean machine, CI) every checkout, merge and `git worktree add` in
this repository exits 127 — which in turn breaks `wl sync` (its
temporary-worktree merge) and `implement.py start`/`finish` worktree creation.
The repository already commits the real script as `.githooks/worklog-post-pull`,
but no wrapper references it.

## Reproduction

```sh
cd /home/rgardler/projects/SorraAgents
# The wrapper hard-codes an absolute path, so the failure is independent of
# $HOME. Simulate a host where that path does not exist by moving the central
# symlink aside for one command (restore it afterwards):
LINK=$HOME/.config/pi/.githooks/worklog-post-pull
mv "$LINK" "$LINK.bak"
git worktree add --detach /tmp/sa-wt-repro HEAD
mv "$LINK.bak" "$LINK"
# → .githooks/post-checkout: 4: exec: /home/rgardler/.config/pi/.githooks/worklog-post-pull: not found
# → rc=127 (verified during intake)
```

On the current agent host the immediate trigger is masked because
`/home/rgardler/.config/pi/.githooks/worklog-post-pull` exists as a symlink to
this repo's committed script (installed by `scripts/install_pi.sh`), so normal
runs here exit 0 ("worklog: sync failed or not initialized; continuing"). The
defect is therefore latent on this host and reproduces on every host or clean
clone where that absolute path is absent.

## Users

- **AI agent driving `/skill:implement`** — needs `implement.py start`/`finish`
  to create worktrees without a hook failure aborting the run.
  Story: *As an implementing agent, when I start work on an item, the worktree
  is created successfully even though the machine has no central hook install.*
- **Agent or developer running `wl sync`** — needs the sync push to complete.
  Story: *As an agent publishing Worklog data, `wl sync` completes its push
  step on a clean clone without setting `WORKLOG_SKIP_POST_PULL=1` or
  `core.hooksPath=/dev/null`.*
- **Developer on a second machine / CI checkout** — needs the committed hooks
  to be portable.
  Story: *As a developer whose username is not `rgardler`, cloning and
  checking out this repository does not emit `exec: ... not found`.*
- **Framework maintainer** — needs the behaviour pinned by a regression test.
  Story: *As a maintainer of the agent framework, I need a test that fails if a
  committed hook regains a hard-coded per-user path.*

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **No hard-coded per-user path.** The three wrappers
      (`.githooks/post-checkout`, `post-merge`, `post-rewrite`) resolve the
      post-pull script without any absolute `/home/<user>` path: they first try
      the repository-relative `<toplevel>/.githooks/worklog-post-pull`, then
      `$HOME/.config/pi/.githooks/worklog-post-pull`, and when neither exists
      they print one clear line to stderr and exit 0 (never 127, never a silent
      failure).
- [ ] **Regression test proving `git worktree add` succeeds.** A hermetic test
      asserts (a) the committed wrappers contain no absolute `/home/<user>` or
      other machine-specific path; (b) in a temp repository built from the
      committed `.githooks/` with `core.hooksPath=.githooks`, a sandboxed
      `$HOME` that has no `.config/pi`, and a stubbed `wl` on `PATH`,
      `git worktree add --detach <tmp> HEAD` exits 0, emits no
      `exec: ... not found`, and reaches the repo-relative
      `.githooks/worklog-post-pull`; and (c) the same setup with
      `worklog-post-pull` absent takes the graceful no-op path (one stderr
      notice naming the attempted locations, `rc=0`, no sync attempted).
- [ ] **`wl sync` completes its push step** in this repository on a host
      without the central hook install (sandboxed `$HOME`), without the
      `WORKLOG_SKIP_POST_PULL=1` / `core.hooksPath=/dev/null` workaround.
- [ ] **Hooks cannot recurse.** A hook-triggered sync from `wl`'s own
      `.worklog/tmp-worktree-*` (and from a linked worktree) exits before
      calling `wl sync`, matching the guards already present in the sibling
      ContextHub/AI_Hell hooks.
- [ ] All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including
      code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries —
      specifically replacing the portability caveat in `docs/dev/worklog-sync.md`
      and updating the `install_pi.sh` fail-open warning to match the new hook
      behaviour.
- [ ] Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Hooks are POSIX `sh` executed by git; they must stay dependency-free (no
  python, no network) and fast, because they run on every checkout/merge.
- `$HOME` and `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` must both be treated as
  best-effort: hook execution inherits git's environment, and earlier incidents
  (SA-0MV0G9BF7008S01K, SA-0MUIZSXEY008NGR8) showed `GIT_DIR`/`GIT_*` pollution
  in spawned sessions. Every resolution step fails open.
- Keep the shared-script model (one implementation in
  `.githooks/worklog-post-pull`) rather than inlining a copy into each wrapper;
  the sibling repositories' self-contained hooks are precedent for the guards,
  not for duplicating sync logic.
- Do not touch the `pre-push` hook behaviour (`worklog:pre-push-hook:v3`) or the
  full-suite gate; this item changes only the post-pull chain.
- Sibling project checkouts (`ContentCreator`, `ContextHub`, `AI_Hell`) are out
  of scope; the ContextHub/AI_Hell copies are reference implementations only,
  and any divergence found there becomes a linked follow-up item.
- Build → test → commit order; no ad-hoc `pytest` — use the test skill /
  `run_tests.py`.
- Preserve the existing bypass variables (`WORKLOG_SKIP_POST_PULL=1`,
  `WORKLOG_SKIP_PRE_PUSH=1`) and their documented semantics.

## Existing state (verified during intake)

- The three wrappers are 184-byte files with header
  `worklog:post-pull-hook:v1` and a single
  `exec "/home/rgardler/.config/pi/.githooks/worklog-post-pull" "$@"` line
  (`.githooks/post-checkout`, `post-merge`, `post-rewrite`).
- `.githooks/worklog-post-pull` **is committed** (514 bytes; runs `wl sync`,
  honours `WORKLOG_SKIP_POST_PULL=1`, fail-open when `wl` is absent). Nothing
  in the repository invokes it: `rg worklog-post-pull` finds only the wrappers'
  hard-coded path, `scripts/install_pi.sh` (central install), one test file and
  the docs.
- `scripts/install_pi.sh` installs the central script as an executable symlink
  to the repo copy (`create_symlink`, idempotent, `PI_SKIP_HOOK_INSTALL=1`
  gated) and then emits a **warning only** when a project's committed wrapper
  does not reference that central path. The warning does not fix the wrapper.
- `docs/dev/worklog-sync.md` (~lines 100–120) documents the delegation and
  carries a "Portability caveat (SA-0MVK1Q30O0067NXX)" paragraph describing
  exactly this defect as unresolved.
- Sibling repositories (`ContextHub`, `AI_Hell`) ship
  self-contained `post-checkout`/`worklog-post-pull` hooks that (a) skip
  `*tmp-worktree-*` paths and (b) skip linked worktrees
  (`git rev-parse --git-dir` vs `--git-common-dir`). The SorraAgents copy of
  `worklog-post-pull` lacks both guards. (`ContentCreator` is reported in the
  consolidated duplicate item to have the same self-contained pattern, but that
  checkout is not present on this host, so it was not verified directly.)
- Verified on this host: `git worktree add --detach /tmp/sa-wt-intake-check HEAD`
  now exits 0 ("worklog: sync failed or not initialized; continuing") because
  the central symlink exists — the hard-coded path is what breaks elsewhere.
- `tests/test_install_pi_post_pull_hook.py` covers the *installer* and writes
  its own synthetic hooks; no test asserts the content or behaviour of this
  repository's committed wrappers.
- `tests/test_install_pi_hook_wiring.py` and `tests/test_pre_push_hook_fallback.py`
  cover the pre-push wiring only.

## Desired change

1. Rewrite the three wrappers to resolve the post-pull script in this order:
   repository-relative (via `git rev-parse --show-toplevel`, falling back to
   `dirname "$0"`), then `$HOME/.config/pi/.githooks/worklog-post-pull`, then a
   single-line stderr notice + `exit 0`. No literal `/home/<user>` anywhere.
2. Add the `*tmp-worktree-*` and linked-worktree guards to
   `.githooks/worklog-post-pull` so a hook-triggered sync cannot nest inside
   `wl sync`'s own temporary worktree, mirroring the sibling implementations.
3. Update the `install_pi.sh` portability warning to reflect the fixed
   behaviour (warning remains a guard for *forked/older* wrappers only).
4. Replace the docs caveat with the actual resolution order and the no-op
   behaviour; document the bypass variables.
5. Add the hermetic regression test described in the ACs.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `.githooks/post-checkout`, `.githooks/post-merge`, `.githooks/post-rewrite` — replace the hard-coded `exec` with portable resolution + graceful no-op.
- `.githooks/worklog-post-pull` — add tmp-worktree and linked-worktree guards; keep `WORKLOG_SKIP_POST_PULL` bypass.
- `scripts/install_pi.sh` — adjust the fail-open portability warning/message to the new contract.
- `docs/dev/worklog-sync.md` — replace the portability caveat with the resolution order and no-op semantics.
- `tests/test_githooks_portability.py` — new hermetic regression tests (worktree add succeeds under a sandboxed `$HOME`; no-op path; bypass; no hard-coded `/home/<user>` in committed hooks).
- `tests/test_install_pi_post_pull_hook.py` — extend only if the installer warning contract changes.

## Related work

- `SA-0MU8CRX1X008IORP` — *Chore: install central wl post-pull hook
  (~/.config/pi/.githooks/worklog-post-pull) missing* (completed): installed the
  central symlink and the wrapper-to-central delegation this item now makes
  portable.
- `SA-0MVK2PK7F002LET6` — *SorraAgents committed git hooks exec a missing
  central script* (closed as duplicate of this item; its reproduction
  transcript, sibling self-contained-hook precedent and `WORKLOG_SKIP_*`
  behaviour are folded in above).
- `SA-0MV8M4OVX000QHSM` — *install_pi.sh propagates the SorraAgents-only test
  gate to non-SorraAgents projects* (completed): precedent for project-vs-framework
  hook variants in the same installer block.
- `SA-0MV0G9BF7008S01K`, `SA-0MUIZSXEY008NGR8` — hook/GIT environment
  investigations that motivate fail-open resolution.
- `SA-0MUJ2VMF7000UHCX` — pre-push git-identity guard (same hook family; do not
  regress it).
- Related docs: `docs/dev/worklog-sync.md`, `docs/dev/worktree-isolation.md`.
- Related files: `.githooks/pre-push` (v3 pattern for `git rev-parse`-based
  resolution), sibling `.githooks/{post-checkout,worklog-post-pull}` in
  `ContextHub`/`AI_Hell`.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Assumption:** repo-relative resolution is the intended shape (the ACs allow
  either repo-relative delegation or inline logic; the repository already
  commits `.githooks/worklog-post-pull`, so reusing it is the minimal change).
- **Assumption:** keeping `$HOME/.config/pi/.githooks/worklog-post-pull` as a
  second candidate preserves compatibility with framework projects whose
  wrappers are installed by `install_pi.sh`.
- **Risk:** `git rev-parse` inside a hook can be misled by `GIT_DIR`/`GIT_*`
  pollution. Mitigation: `2>/dev/null`, fall back to `dirname "$0"`, then
  `$HOME`, then no-op.
- **Risk:** a no-op can hide a broken install. Mitigation: the stderr line names
  both attempted paths and points at `scripts/install_pi.sh`.
- **Risk:** the new test could invoke real `wl` (network/sync side effects).
  Mitigation: sandboxed `$HOME`, stub `wl` on `PATH`, or assert the no-op path
  only; never perform a real sync in the test.
- **Scope-creep risk:** rewriting hooks in sibling repositories, redesigning
  `wl sync`, or changing the pre-push gate are out of scope; record as linked
  follow-up items.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

No clarifying questions were asked in this intake: the seed brief, the
reproduction transcript from the consolidated duplicate, and repository
inspection supplied enough detail to draft an unambiguous brief.

Research performed (evidence links):

- Q (self-resolved): "Does the repository already contain the post-pull
  script?" — Answer: **yes**, `.githooks/worklog-post-pull` is committed
  (514 bytes) but unreferenced by the wrappers. Evidence: `rg worklog-post-pull`;
  file contents.
- Q (self-resolved): "Why does the failure not appear on this host?" — Answer:
  the wrappers hard-code `/home/rgardler`, and on this host the
  `scripts/install_pi.sh` install (`SA-0MU8CRX1X008IORP`) provides that exact
  path as a symlink to the repo script, so checkout succeeds and the defect is
  latent. Removing the symlink for one command reproduces `rc=127`; changing
  `$HOME` alone does not, because the path is absolute. Evidence:
  `mv …/worklog-post-pull …; git worktree add …; mv back` (verified during
  intake), `ls -la ~/.config/pi/.githooks`.
- Q (self-resolved): "Is there a precedent implementation?" — Answer: **yes**,
  `ContextHub` and `AI_Hell` ship self-contained post-checkout hooks with
  `*tmp-worktree-*` and linked-worktree guards. Evidence: sibling `.githooks/`
  contents (`ContentCreator` not present on this host).
- Q (self-resolved): "Is the defect already tested?" — Answer: **no**.
  `tests/test_install_pi_post_pull_hook.py` tests the installer with synthetic
  hooks; nothing asserts the committed wrappers. Evidence: `rg` over `tests/`.
- Duplicate check performed: `wl search "post-pull hook"` / `"worklog hook"`
  found `SA-0MVK2PK7F002LET6` (same defect), closed as a duplicate of this item;
  no other overlapping open or completed item found.

### Related work items
- **SA-0MVK2PK7F002LET6** – SorraAgents committed git hooks exec a missing central script (~/.config/pi/.githooks/worklog-post-pull) (completed)
- **SA-0MU8CRX1X008IORP** – Chore: install central wl post-pull hook (~/.config/pi/.githooks/worklog-post-pull) missing (completed)
- **SA-0MV0G9BF7008S01K** – GIT_DIR evidence: trace non-destructive env propagation path (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — matched: aborting, absent, absolute, acceptance, acs (+344 more)
- `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` — matched: absent, absolute, acceptance, acs, actual (+314 more)

# Finish gate: test the tree the commit produces, and prove every verdict's provenance

## Objective

Make `implement.py finish`'s test gate validate the exact tree the commit
will produce, and make every gate verdict self-describing (which tree ran,
whether it came from cache). A green gate must never again be produced by a
suite run against a different tree or by a stale cached result.

## Problem statement

`phase_finish` runs the test gate **before** it stages and commits
(`git_commit` performs `git add -A` afterwards). Suite tests that key off the
**tracked** file set (`git ls-files`) therefore cannot see files the commit is
about to add, and the gate can report a green full-scope run for a tree that
is red the moment the commit lands. The false green is silent: the report says
"full scope, success", so no agent looks further, and the tree stays red at
the push, in CI, and for the next agent.

Observed on ContentCreator work item **OSL-0MVK2F1Z300996SA** (Ep 1 of *Inside
the Content Creation Suite*):

- `implement.py finish` reported `{"tooling": "suite", "scope": "full",
  "success": true}` and pushed commit `9c88625c`.
- A full-suite run on the same tree immediately after reported **2 failed**,
  both caused by the newly added files:
  - `test_no_podcast_episode_content_tracked_outside_documented_leftovers` —
    `podcasts/ep1-why-use-it/*` were not yet in `git ls-files`, so the
    allowlist guard passed pre-commit and failed post-commit.
  - `test_registry_documents_match_on_disk_documents` — the wiki registry was
    stale for the new synthesis page. This test reads **on-disk** files, not
    `git ls-files`, so untracked-invisibility cannot explain its false pass.
- The item was re-finished (`9f3a1f6c`) after fixing the allowlist and
  rebuilding the metadata; the suite was green at that commit
  (`2765 passed, 16 skipped`). The defect is the false green, not the fix.

Origin record: **OSL-0MVKT9LN10097FA2** (ContentCreator worklog) — full intake
brief, investigation trail, and evidence.

## Investigation findings (from the origin intake)

Two mechanisms are supported; both must be closed:

1. **Untracked-file invisibility (proved).** `git_commit` stages *after* the
   test step, and the suite runs against the loose working tree. Anything
   using `git ls-files` semantics cannot see the commit's new files.
2. **Verdict may not correspond to a suite run at the gate's tree (root
   cause to pin).** Surviving cache evidence: the nearest green full-suite
   entry in the shared `.worklog/cache` (08:53, state `8e9c3ea7…`) collected
   **2751** tests, i.e. the dev tree before the episode work's test files
   existed; the post-commit red run (10:56, `f73d063e…`) collected **2781**,
   matching the committed tree. The gate's own per-worktree cache was deleted
   with the worktree, so the exact entry served cannot be recovered. Because
   the parity test reads disk, untracked-invisibility alone cannot explain its
   pass: the gate either executed against a different checkout/state or served
   a cached result recorded for a different tree.

## Desired change

1. **Temporary-index gate (operator-approved option A).** Before the gate's
   test step: copy the real index to a temp file, apply the change set to the
   copy (`GIT_INDEX_FILE=<tmp> git add -A`), and run the suite with
   `GIT_INDEX_FILE` exported so every child `git` command (including
   `git ls-files` inside tests) sees the staged file set. On success the real
   index receives `git add -A` and the commit proceeds; on failure the temp
   index is deleted and the real index and working tree are untouched.
   `GIT_INDEX_FILE` is currently **not** in `REPOSITORY_OVERRIDE_ENV_VARS`
   (`skill/shared/git_sandbox.py`), so it survives the runner's env scrub —
   this must be asserted by a regression test so a future scrub addition
   cannot silently break the fix.
2. **Verifiable verdicts.** The gate's report must state (a) the tree the
   suite ran against (worktree path + git fingerprint) and (b) whether the
   result was served from the cache. A cached verdict is acceptable only when
   its fingerprint is the would-be-commit tree's fingerprint; otherwise the
   suite must run.

Rejected: stage-then-test with unstage-on-abort (mutates the real index,
fragile restore); `git status --porcelain`-clean assertion only (demands a
clean tree and still does not test the commit's file set).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **Gate tests the would-be commit tree:** a change set that adds a file
      rejected by a tracked-file guard (`git ls-files` semantics) fails the
      finish gate, with the failing test named, instead of reporting a green
      full-scope pass. Reproduced through the finish-gate entry point.
- [ ] **The gate proves its verdict:** the report records the tree it ran
      against (worktree path + fingerprint) and whether the result came from
      cache; no green verdict is accepted for a state whose suite has not run
      (stale/foreign cache entries must miss).
- [ ] **Abort leaves the tree unchanged:** on gate failure there is no partial
      commit, no residual staging, and the temporary index is removed.
- [ ] **Cache determinism:** `GIT_INDEX_FILE` passes through the test skill's
      env scrub into child git commands (regression test), and the gate's
      cache key reflects the would-be-commit tree, not the loose working tree.
- [ ] **Existing green runs unaffected:** a clean change set passes exactly as
      today with a single gate suite execution (no duplicate run).
- [ ] **Parity false pass explained:** the regression work reproduces the
      disk-reading parity case at the finish-gate entry point and records the
      root cause (wrong checkout / stale cache / metadata lag before staging)
      in this work item.
- [ ] **Testing/validation:** the framework suites pass —
      `skill/implement/tests/`, `skill/test/tests/`, `tests/test_test_cache.py`,
      plus the repository full suite at the dev-push gate.
- [ ] **Documentation:** `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` (finish gate
      semantics, verdict provenance), `docs/dev/test-skill-reference.md`
      (cache fingerprint / `GIT_INDEX_FILE` contract) updated. CHANGELOG.md is
      managed by the ship skill and excluded.

## Constraints

- ✗ Do not weaken the gate: no default bypasses (`TEST_SCOPE_SKIP` etc.);
  guard ownership (`LIVE_REPO_GUARD_ACTIVE`) and the nested-run stand-down
  contract stay intact.
- ✗ One suite execution per gate verdict on a clean change set.
- ✗ The changed-scope development gate stays the fast path; the full suite
  stays the dev-push integration gate.
- ✗ Implemented in this repository (framework); do not edit the global install
  directly.

## Key Files

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — `phase_finish` test step,
  `git_commit`, `_run_resolved_suite` / `_run_guarded_suite`, gate report keys.
- `skill/test_cache.py` — `compute_git_state` / `run_cached` / `cache_dir`.
- `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` — `guarded_run_all`, env construction
  (`subprocess_env_with_scrubbed_overrides`).
- `skill/shared/git_sandbox.py` — `REPOSITORY_OVERRIDE_ENV_VARS`.
- `skill/implement/tests/test_implement_guard_ownership.py`,

  regression-test homes.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk:** a temporary index changes *staged* status, which may surprise
  tests asserting on working-tree state beyond `git ls-files` (e.g.
  `git ls-files --error-unmatch` in ContentCreator's
  `test_implement_state_gitignore.py`). Mitigation: re-verify such tests in
  the regression work and document the semantics.
- **Risk:** two cache entries per state (loose vs staged fingerprint);
  accepted — correctness over hit ratio.
- **Assumption:** the parity false pass shares the gate-to-tree mismatch
  cause rather than a metadata-lag-only cause; the reproduction settles it.
- **Cross-repo note:** project-level fallout (ContentCreator's missing

# implement.py drive livelocks when phase_parent repeatedly fails to finish a child (no recovery from finishing_failed)

## Headline

`implement.py drive` can loop forever without the epic ever advancing when `phase_parent` repeatedly fails to `finish` the same non-terminal child (its abandoned worktree keeps tripping the `finishing_failed` path); drive must bound finish attempts, reconcile the child's actual state, and recover to a clean startable state instead of re-running the identical failing `finish` on every invocation.

## Problem statement

When a driven child session dies mid-work (timeout, host load), its worktree is left dirty and its item non-terminal. `phase_parent` classifies the dirty worktree as "has changes" and runs `implement.py finish <child>`; `finish` fails (build/tests red on the abandoned WIP) and resets the child status to `open` but leaves the worktree dirty. `phase_drive` then aborts the whole chain with `"Failed to finish child …"` (`finishing_failed`, `sessions_spawned: 0`), and the next drive invocation repeats the identical `finish` failure. Nothing bounds the retries or resets the child, so the epic never advances.

Observed 2026-10-19 driving epic AH-0MV9DB68T002IROX ("Compile an action video"): 29+ drive runs, each exiting 1 after 600–890 s with `Failed to finish child AH-0MVDV4PNZ004ZWOZ`, `sessions_spawned: 0`, `parent_advanced: false` (evidence: `/tmp/epic_resilient_drive.log`). Terminal children are already handled: `_classify_child` returns `skip-terminal` for `completed`/`done`/`in_review`/deleted and never reaches the worktree/finish path — so the recorded framing "drive must treat terminal children as done" is not the reproducible defect (intake Q1 → re-scoped, producer-confirmed).

## Users

- **Producers / herdr downtime dispatcher** driving epics: needs `drive` to terminate reliably and advance the epic once children are done — not burn 15 minutes per run on the same failing `finish`.
- **Epic owner / auditor** reading `drive --json` output: a truthful report that distinguishes "finished", "terminal-reconciled", and "reset for fresh session" instead of a bare `Failed to finish child`.
- **Child owner** whose session was killed: auto-recovery must not silently discard *their* progress without a recorded comment and a clean restart path.

Example user stories:

- *As a producer driving an epic unattended,* I want `implement.py drive` to terminate within one bounded cycle per child, so an abandoned dirty worktree cannot stall the epic for 29 runs.
- *As an epic auditor,* I want `drive --json` to tell me whether a child was finished, reconciled as terminal, or reset for a fresh session, so `parent_advanced: false` always means real work remains.
- *As the owner of a child whose session was killed,* I want a comment recording why my worktree was reset, so my WIP is never discarded silently.

## Acceptance Criteria

- 1. **Bounded finish attempts.** `phase_drive`/`phase_parent` counts failed `finish` executions per child; the same child's failing `finish` is never run unboundedly (limit configurable, defaulting to the existing per-child session cap). Unit-testable with a fake `parent_runner` that always reports `finishing_failed` for one child.
- 2. **Terminal-state reconciliation.** When a child's `finish` has exhausted its attempts (or the child is found terminal at any point), drive re-fetches the child via `wl show`: if the child is terminal (`completed`/`done` status or `in_review` stage, or soft-deleted), it is recorded as done (`ok`), never reset, and drive continues to the next actionable child.
- 3. **Non-terminal recovery, no livelock.** A non-terminal child whose `finish` failed is reset to a clean startable state — item status `open` via the shared `StatusLifecycle` path and its worktree reset to the parent-branch HEAD (`git reset --hard <parent-branch>` + `git clean -fd`) with a recorded comment naming the failure reason — after which drive continues and the next iteration starts a fresh session for it. `parent_advanced` reflects the true state (false only when non-terminal/blocked work genuinely remains). Reproducing the AH-0MV9DB68T002IROX scenario must terminate with the epic advancing.
- 4. **Truthful report.** Per-child `children_driven` entries / failure reasons distinguish `finished`, `terminal-reconciled`, and `reset-for-retry` (with evidence: child status/stage, failure summary).
- 5. **Terminal children never touched.** A child already in a terminal stage is never `finished`, reset, or re-spawned (regression guard; the existing `skip-terminal` precedence is preserved and covered by a test).
- 6. **Tests pass.** New unit tests cover: bounded-finish-attempts, finish-failure→terminal reconciliation, finish-failure→non-terminal reset+continue, terminal-child regression, and truthful reporting (drive-loop fixtures with injectable `parent_runner`/`spawn_session`). Existing `skill/implement/tests/` drive/parent tests continue to pass.
- 7. **Documentation updated.** `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` (and any README/wiki entries describing `drive`'s failure handling) reflect the bounded-recovery behaviour, including the recovery tiers and their audit comments.
- 8. **Full suite green.** The full project test suite passes with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Preserve session-per-child isolation, per-child worktree semantics, and dependency-order driving (SA-0MTLCCIPU0050Q52, SA-0MUWNHKQH0034DW9); the drive recursion guard is retained.
- Never reset, finish, or re-spawn an already-terminal child; reset operations touch only the child's own worktree (never the main checkout) and always leave an audit comment on the child.
- `parent_advanced` must stay `false` while any real non-terminal/blocked child work remains; the parent advances only when every child is terminal.
- The recovery mutation (status `open` + worktree reset) is bounded and explicit — no silent discarding of WIP without the recorded reason.

## Existing state

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py`:
  - `phase_parent` (~4978) — the parent-recursion loop; `_run_finish` (~5209) sets `success: false`, `finishing_failed: true`, `next_child` and returns `None` on any finish-subprocess failure; `_classify_child` (~807) already returns `skip-terminal` for terminal children.
  - `phase_drive` (~5620) — breaks the chain on `parent_report["success"] is False` (`~5765`) with no attempt accounting for finish failures and no reconciliation; `attempts` only increments on spawned sessions (`~5546`).
  - `_invoke_implement` (~4903), `_has_worktree_changes` (`~4966`), `_git_path_has_changes` (`~5909`).
- `skill/shared/status_lifecycle.py` — `StatusLifecycle.update_status` (`~614`), `require_claimed`/`ensure_claimed` (`~664/707`) — reuse for the reset path.
- `skill/implement/tests/test_drive_child_session.py` — spawner-command tests only; no drive-loop fixtures covering `finishing_failed` or terminal reconciliation.
- `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` — documents `drive`'s session/extension mechanics; no recovery/termination semantics section for finish failures.

## Desired change

In `phase_drive` (and minimal support in `phase_parent`'s report), replace the immediate-break-on-`finishing_failed` with a bounded recovery loop per child: (1) count the failing finish; (2) when the bound is hit, re-fetch the child via `wl show` and classify with `_is_terminal_child`; (3) terminal → record as done, continue; non-terminal → comment + reset (status `open` + worktree reset to parent-branch HEAD, gated on worktree isolation checks) and continue so the next loop iteration starts a fresh session. Emit truthful per-child results. Add the discard/reset helper with an explicit audit comment and tests.

## Key Files

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — `phase_drive` (recovery loop), `phase_parent`/`_run_finish` (failure reporting), new worktree-reset helper, `_classify_child` guard reuse.
- `skill/implement/tests/` — new drive-recovery tests (e.g. `test_drive_recovery.py`), fixtures with fake `parent_runner`/`spawn_session`.
- `skill/shared/status_lifecycle.py` — status reset/finalise path for the recovery mutation.
- `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` — document bounded-recovery + truthful reporting.
- `scripts/install_pi.sh` — reinstall step (post-implementation) because the canonical source is this repo's `skill/` tree.

## Related work

- SA-0MUWNHKQH0034DW9 (completed) — drive all epic children to completion (fresh session per child).
- SA-0MTLCCIPU0050Q52 (completed) — session-per-child for epics.
- SA-0MUY9PYBD009Y7J5 (completed) — driven-child session boundary error fix.
- SA-0MVHXWLPG007OQVN (open) — drive reports child failed on session timeout without terminal-state reconciliation: overlapping in spirit (drive does not reconcile child state), but covers the spawn-timeout path, not the `finishing_failed` path here; keep separate, cross-link.
- AH-0MVFBCVIS007BN81 (open, AI_Hell) — behind-only child worktree mis-detected as "has changes": the mis-detection feeds the same `has_changes → finish` entry into the livelock; keep separate (detection bug vs recovery gap), cross-link.
- AH-0MVFNYAOB003PDLA (AI_Hell) — seed tracker; `discovered-from` provenance; deleted per operator decision once this item was created.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption A1.** The reproduced livelock is entirely attributable to the unbounded `finishing_failed` retry with no reconciliation/reset; the dirty-worktree detection (`_git_path_has_changes`) is handled by AH-0MVFBCVIS007BN81 and is out of scope here.
- **Assumption A2.** Resetting a failed child's worktree is acceptable *only* with an audit comment and only after the finish bound is exhausted — it must never run for terminal children or children whose work landed outside the worktree.
- **Risk R1.** The worktree reset could discard legitimate WIP if a finish failure was transient (flaky test). Mitigation: bound attempts before reset; keep the failing `finish` output in the comment; prefer `reset --hard <parent-branch>` only in the child's own worktree (never `git clean` on shared paths).
- **Risk R2.** Reconciliation re-fetches child state on the slow failure path only; no added latency on the happy path.
- **Risk R3.** Scope creep into the timeout-reconciliation (SA-0MVHXWLPG007OQVN) or detection (AH-0MVFBCVIS007BN81) items. Mitigation: cross-link rather than absorb; keep ACs focused on the `finishing_failed` loop.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "Re-scope the problem statement to the evidence-based root cause (repeated `finishing_failed` on an abandoned dirty worktree), keep it as written (terminal children), or both?" — Answer (operator, interactive): A — re-scope; terminal handling kept only as a regression guard. Source: interactive reply in this intake (AH-0MVFNYAOB003PDLA session). Research: `_classify_child` (`implement.py:807`) already returns `skip-terminal` before any worktree inspection, so "drive must treat terminal children as done" alone would not change behaviour.
- Q2: "Recovery policy when `finish` fails for a non-terminal child: bounded attempts + reset to clean startable state (A), immediate actionable stop (B), or auto-finalise if pushed to dev (C)?" — Answer (operator): A. Source: interactive reply. Research: today `finish` on failure resets status to `open` but leaves the dirty worktree, so the next `parent` run re-runs `finish` — the exact unbounded loop (evidence `/tmp/epic_resilient_drive.log`); option A breaks it while B is the status quo that livelocked.

Source: interactive reply. Research: the installed `~/.pi/agent/skills/implement/scripts/implement.py` is byte-identical to `SorraAgents/skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` (deploy target); AGENTS.md repo-boundary rule prohibits direct edits of installed skill trees. AH-0MVFNYAOB003PDLA deleted after this item's creation per operator instruction; provenance recorded above.

# Intake Brief — Drive epic children in interactive Herdr panes

## Problem statement

`implement.py drive <parent>` (`phase_drive`, SA-0MUWNHKQH0034DW9) runs each
child's fresh Pi session as a **headless subprocess**:

```
pi -p "/skill:implement <child>" --approve --no-extensions
```

with `capture_output=True`. The operator therefore has:

- no view of the child session while it runs (only the parent's own progress
  lines and `wait_for_job` heartbeats);
- no ability to watch the agent work, scroll its transcript, or intervene when
  it stalls, hits an approval/question boundary, or loops;
- no evidence after a failure beyond a 5-line `_tail_lines(...)` summary of
  captured stderr/stdout;
- no per-child terminal artefact to point at during review.

An operator running an epic in Herdr already watches a grid of interactive
`π` TUI panes for other work. Drive should produce the same kind of pane —
one interactive Pi TUI session per child, opened as a sibling pane in the
caller's tab — so the epic runs *visibly*.

A headless-in-a-pane variant (option A: `pane split` + `pane run` +
exit-sentinel) was evaluated and rejected as insufficient: it shows log text,
not a browsable/typeable Pi TUI session, and offers no session-level state.

## Users

- **Operator / producer driving an epic from a Herdr-managed Pi session.**
  - *User story:* "As an operator, when I run `implement.py drive <epic>`, I
    want each child implemented in its own interactive Pi TUI pane inside the
    tab I invoked from, so I can watch progress, scroll the full transcript,
    and step in if a child stalls — without leaving my own session."
- **Reviewer / auditor.** *User story:* "As a reviewer, I want each child's
  session transcript to still be inspectable after drive finishes, so I can
  check what the agent actually did."

## Goal

`implement.py drive <parent>` opens **each** child's implementation session as
an interactive Pi TUI agent in a new pane split from the calling pane (same
tab), drives that pane's lifecycle to completion, and continues the existing
serial/blocking-order/parent-last loop — preserving session isolation,
worktree isolation, error isolation, and the recursion guard.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Pane-per-child in the caller's tab.** For each startable child, drive
   runs `herdr pane split` from the invoking pane (no `tab create`, no
   `workspace create`) with `--cwd <child worktree>` and returns the new pane
   id from `.result.pane.pane_id`; the child Pi TUI is started in that pane via
   `herdr agent start <name> --kind pi --pane <id> -- --approve
   --no-extensions` and prompted with `/skill:implement <child_id>` via
   `herdr agent prompt ... --wait`. Verified by a test that asserts the herdr
   CLI invocations (split/prompt/wait/close) and asserts no tab/workspace
   creation call is made.
2. **Driver waits on session state, not process exit.** Completion of a child
   is determined by (a) `herdr agent wait <name> --until done|blocked` for the
   pane-side signal and (b) the existing `phase_parent` re-read of the work
   item's stage as the authoritative signal. Drive never assumes an
   interactive agent process exits when the work item completes. Tests cover
   the `done`, `blocked`, and timeout transitions.
3. **Blocked children are reported, not silently abandoned.** When an agent
   reports `blocked` (approval/question UI), drive stops the chain, records the
   child id and the pane id in the JSON report (`blocked_child`,
   `blocked_pane`), leaves the pane open for the operator, and emits actionable
   text naming the pane. Tested with a fake herdr runner.
4. **No orphaned sessions:** a pane created by drive is either (a) closed once
   its child reaches a terminal stage and the child's session was clean, or
   (b) explicitly retained and reported (blocked/failed) — never leaked
   silently. Unit tests assert a close call per successful child and no close
   call for blocked/failed children.
5. **Opt-in with fail-open fallback.** Pane driving activates only when
   Herdr is detected (`HERDR_ENV=1` and a resolvable herdr binary) **and** the
   operator opted in (`--pane-sessions`, or `IMPLEMENT_DRIVE_PANE_SESSIONS=1`).
   Otherwise the existing `_default_session_spawner` headless path is used
   unchanged. Tests cover herdr-absent, opt-out, and herdr-present paths.
6. **Environment isolation is preserved for pane children.** The child process
   receives `IMPLEMENT_DRIVE_ACTIVE=1`, `IMPLEMENT_WORKTREE_PATH=<worktree>`,
   and does **not** inherit `PI_SESSION_ID` / `PI_SESSION_FILE` from the
   driving session (assert the constructed env / pane-split `--env` args and
   the `env -u` prefix). Recursion guard and per-child worktree enforcement
   continue to work inside the pane.
7. **Timeouts and iteration bounds are enforced across the new transport.**
   `IMPLEMENT_DRIVE_CHILD_TIMEOUT` (and the existing per-child session bound
   `--max-child-sessions`) still bound the wait; a timeout closes the pane,
   records `reason`, and stops the chain as today. Tested with a fake clock /
   fake herdr wait returning `timeout`.
8. **Focus behaviour.** Default is `--no-focus` so the caller's focus is
   unchanged; an explicit `--focus` variant switches to each new child pane.
   Assert the flag passed to `pane split` in both modes.
9. **Report parity.** Human and `--json` reports keep the existing shape and
   gain `pane_id` per driven child plus `transport: "pane" | "headless"`; the
   final summary lists panes retained for inspection. Tests assert the new
   fields and that existing fields are unchanged (no breaking change for
   consumers of the drive report).
10. **Docs.** `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` (drive section) and
    `skill/implement/SKILL.md` Step 6.1 document: pane-per-child behaviour, the
    opt-in flag/env var, focus behaviour, blocked-child handling (which pane to
    look at, and that it is intentionally left open), and the headless fallback
    for non-Herdr/automated callers.
11. **Build, tests, and full suite.** Changed-scope tests pass before commit;
    the dev-push full-suite gate is green.

## Design sketch (non-binding)

- Add `_pane_session_spawner(child_id, worktree_path, timeout, env, verbose)`
  next to `_default_session_spawner`, returning the same
  `{"success", "returncode", "reason"}` shape plus `pane_id`.
- Extract herdr CLI calls into a small injectable helper (reuse the fail-open
  style of `skill/shared/herdr_pane.py`; do not duplicate its `HERDR_BIN_PATH`
  resolution logic — reuse or import it) so tests fake the CLI boundary with
  no live Herdr.
- In `phase_drive`, select the spawner by transport: existing injection point
  (`spawn_session`) already allows tests to bypass either; the CLI path chooses
  pane vs headless from the opt-in + detection check.
- Agent naming: `drive-<child-id-lowercased>` (herdr names must match
  `[a-z][a-z0-9_-]{0,31}`, unique among live agents) — truncation/validation
  must be tested.
- Pane labelling: on completion/failure, set the pane title via the existing
  `herdr_pane.update_pane_title(status, pane_id=...)` helper so the retained
  pane carries its verdict.

## Constraints

- Do not change the session-per-child rule (SA-0MTLCCIPU0050Q52), worktree
  isolation, dependency ordering, or parent-advanced-last semantics — all live
  above the spawner.
- Do not change `_default_session_spawner` behaviour for automated callers
  (downtime worker, audit dispatch, CI): headless `pi -p` must remain the
  default outside Herdr.
- No edits to the repo-external Herdr agent skill or the installed
  `~/.pi/agent/extensions/` files (herdr-managed).
- `herdr agent start` requires the pane to be at an interactive shell prompt;
  the implementation must handle `agent_not_ready` (retry within the existing
  timeout or fail with a reported reason), not crash.
- Herdr CLI failures must be fail-open at the boundary (recorded reason,
  chain stops cleanly) — never leave the epic in an unrecoverable state.

## Risks & mitigations

- **Loss of the process-exit completion signal.** An interactive TUI session
  does not exit when the work item completes, so completion must come from
  wl stage + `agent wait`. *Mitigation:* AC 2 makes `phase_parent` the
  authority (it already is) and `agent wait` only a fast-path; covered by tests.
- **Pane/session leakage.** Panes and interactive agents persist after drive
  ends. *Mitigation:* AC 4 explicit close-or-report rule, plus pane-title
  verdict marking for retained panes.
- **Serial drive + visible panes can be noisy.** One pane open at a time,
  closed on success. *Mitigation:* documented; failure/blocked panes retained
  deliberately.
- **Herdr API drift** (JSON shapes, kind list, name rules). *Mitigation:*
  single injected helper for CLI calls; parse ids defensively; fail open.
- **Approval prompts could block an unattended epic.** *Mitigation:* start
  with `--approve` and treat `blocked` as an explicit, reported stop (AC 3).

## Existing state

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — `phase_drive`, `phase_parent`,
  `_child_session_env`, `_default_session_spawner`, `_resolve_child_session_timeout`,
  `_resolve_pi_bin`, `_emit_phase_report`; `--max-child-sessions` and
  `--child-timeout` CLI flags; `spawn_session` injection point.
- `tests/test_implement_drive.py` — deterministic orchestration tests with
  `ScriptedParent` / `RecordingSpawner`; `skill/implement/tests/test_drive_child_session.py`
  — spawer/env tests.
- `skill/shared/herdr_pane.py` — fail-open Herdr CLI helper (`HERDR_BIN_PATH`,
  `pane list`/`pane rename`, status prefix/truncation, `update_pane_title`).
- Herdr CLI surface (verified against the installed binary): `pane split
  --current --direction right|down --cwd --env --no-focus`, `pane run`,
  `pane wait-output`, `pane read`, `pane close`, `pane rename`,
  `agent start <name> --kind pi --pane <id> [-- args]`, `agent prompt
  <target> <text> --wait [--until] [--timeout]`, `agent wait`, `agent get`,
  `agent list`, `agent read`. Caller context env: `HERDR_ENV`,
  `HERDR_WORKSPACE_ID`, `HERDR_TAB_ID`, `HERDR_PANE_ID`.

## Appendix: decisions from the discovery conversation

- Transport choice: **option B** (interactive Pi TUI agent in a pane) over
  option A (headless `pi -p` run in a pane, exit-sentinel + `pane read`).
  Rationale recorded: option A shows log text only; B gives a browsable,
  typeable session and Herdr's lifecycle states, at the cost of replacing the
  process-exit completion signal with wl-stage + `agent wait` (AC 2).
- Opt-in rather than default: automated callers (downtime worker, audit
  dispatch, CI) have no Herdr and must keep the headless path (AC 5).
- Forked-decision for planning: whether to factor the herdr CLI boundary into a
  shared module (`skill/shared/`) or keep it local to `implement.py`; prefer
  reuse of `herdr_pane.py`'s resolution/fail-open conventions either way.

## Related work

- **SA-0MUWNHKQH0034DW9** — implement skill: drive all epic children to
  completion (fresh session per child) — the headless drive this item extends.
- **SA-0MUWBHEEF002A6BO** — When running implement on a parent item implement
  all children — original one-invocation drive requirement.
- **SA-0MTLCCIPU0050Q52** — When implementing an epic start a new session for
  each child — session isolation rule that must be preserved.
- **SA-0MVDQF3VW002PKCA** — User-visible progress feedback during long-running
  waits — related observability work for drive runs.
- **SA-0MTFLQEQQ0083EW1** — Update pane title with status emoticon on skill
  completion — reuse `herdr_pane.update_pane_title` for retained panes.

# Worktree `@worklog/shared` resolves to the main checkout's stale `dist`

## Problem statement

In an `implement.py` worktree, every `@worklog/shared` import (tests, `src/**`,
spawned CLI subprocesses) resolves through the worktree's `node_modules`
symlink to the **main checkout's** `packages/shared/dist`, so a branch that
changes `packages/shared/src/**` is invisible to the build/test gate: correct
new code fails the gate (false red — observed in ContextHub
WL-0MVK6S4HM005GBCO) and a genuinely broken shared change can pass (false
green).

## Users

**Primary:** agents (and the humans reviewing their work) running the implement
workflow in a worktree of a repo with a workspace package that is consumed by
path (ContextHub's `packages/shared` is the reference case).

- As an agent implementing an item that touches `packages/shared/src/**`, I
  want the sanctioned gate to exercise the code in my worktree, so a green
  result means my change is correct and a red result names my change.
- As a producer reviewing an `in_review` item, I want the gate result in the
  work-item record to be trustworthy — not a false green, not a false red.
- As an agent starting a fresh worktree, I want the supported setup to be
  automatic or one documented command, so I neither rediscover the `rsync`
  workaround nor "fix" the symptom by weakening tests.

## Root cause (verified)

1. `implement.py start` symlinks `<worktree>/node_modules ->
   <main-checkout>/node_modules` (`_ensure_node_modules_symlink`,
   SA-0MSGS763C006SM1B), and mirrors nested workspace `node_modules`
   directories (`_ensure_nested_node_modules_symlinks`, OSL-0MUFG3PJA00379CT).
2. `<main-checkout>/node_modules/@worklog/shared` is itself a relative symlink
   `../../packages/shared` — the **main checkout's** shared package.
3. `packages/shared/package.json` `main`/`exports` point at `./dist/*.js`
   (gitignored build output).
4. `npm run build` (or `build:shared`) inside the worktree rebuilds the
   **worktree's** `packages/shared/dist`, which nothing in the worktree
   resolves to; only `packages/shared/src/*.test.ts` (relative imports) see the
   change.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Worktree-local resolution.** After `implement.py start` (and after any
   refresh step it performs), `@worklog/shared` resolves to
   `<worktree>/packages/shared` — verified by an automated test asserting the
   resolved package root, and end-to-end by a probe change in a fresh
   worktree's `packages/shared/src/**` that the sanctioned gate
   (`run_tests.py --type full --scope full`) observes and an unmodified main
   checkout would not.
2. **Link-farm `node_modules`.** The worktree's `node_modules` is a real
   directory of per-entry symlinks into the main checkout's `node_modules`
   (nested scopes materialised per package, `.bin` linked as a whole), with
   `@worklog/shared` overridden to the worktree's workspace package. The step
   is idempotent, refreshable when the main checkout's dependency set changes,
   and reported in the `start` JSON report.
3. **No cross-checkout contamination.** No writes pass through the
   `node_modules` symlink into the main checkout's `node_modules`; the main
   checkout stays git-clean apart from gitignored build artefacts after
   start → build → gate → finish from a worktree. The main checkout's own
   build/test behaviour is unchanged.
4. **Hard-fail on stale resolution.** `implement.py finish` (build → test gate)
   fails with an actionable message naming the stale
   `<main-checkout>/packages/shared/dist` path when the worktree changes
   `packages/shared/src/**` while `@worklog/shared` still resolves outside the
   worktree — covered by a test for the detection helper and by a
   negative-path test that the gate cannot silently pass on the main checkout's
   `dist`.
5. **Constraint honoured.** The documented ban on `npm install` inside a
   worktree stays in force and the fix does not require installing into the
   worktree; the option of `rsync`-ing the worktree's shared `dist` into the
   main checkout is explicitly rejected (it mutates the `dist` that the live
   `wl` CLI and every concurrent worktree execute — the WL-0MQRBT8BS00355AB
   class of incident).
6. **Documentation.** The implement skill's worktree section
   (`skill/implement/SKILL.md`) and `implement.py` docstrings describe the
   link-farm resolution order, the refresh/re-run command, the stale-resolution
   failure signature (e.g. the "spy never called" false red), and the
   prohibition on `npm install` in worktrees.

## Constraints

- **Repository:** implementation lives in SorraAgents (`skill/implement/`):
  `implement.py` (`_ensure_node_modules_symlink` ~L1638,
  `_ensure_nested_node_modules_symlinks` ~L1735, `run_build`/finish build step
  ~L4432, `finish` gate) and `skill/implement/SKILL.md` (~L547–558).
- **Do not install into worktrees.** `npm install`/`npm ci` inside a worktree
  is forbidden: writes would pass through the symlinked tree and corrupt the
  shared install.
- **Do not mutate the main checkout's `dist`.** Refreshing
  `<main-checkout>/packages/shared/dist` from a worktree changes what the live
  `wl` CLI and all other agents execute, and lets concurrent worktrees clobber
  each other; a lock does not make it safe, only slower.
- **Cross-platform:** the current symlink step is POSIX-first; if linking
  directories on Windows needs junctions, follow the precedent in ContextHub's
  `packages/herdr/scripts/link-shared.mjs` (junction on Windows, relative
  symlink elsewhere) and keep the failure non-fatal there.
- **Never weaken tests** to make the gate pass; the false red must be fixed in
  tooling, not by reducing assertions (the exact temptation recorded in
  WL-0MVK6S4HM005GBCO).
- **Fail-open vs fail-closed:** the *link step* stays non-fatal (usable
  worktree on tooling edge cases); the *staleness detection* in `finish` is
  fail-closed once the worktree diff touches shared source.
- Behaviour change is confined to worktree setups; the main checkout path is
  byte-for-byte unchanged.

## Existing state

- The `node_modules` auto-symlink and its verification are documented in
  ContextHub `docs/dev/implement-worktree-node-modules-verification.md`
  (WL-0MSGQ64N2006TQB2): the symlink fixed missing-`node_modules` failures but
  introduced this resolution hop.
- ContextHub `packages/herdr/scripts/link-shared.mjs` (`linkSharedPackage()`)
  already replaces a stale packaged copy of `@worklog/shared` with a relative
  symlink to the live workspace package — the same pattern this fix applies at
  the worktree root.
- Current manual workaround (used by WL-0MVK6S4HM005GBCO): build
  `packages/shared` in the worktree, then
  `rsync -a --delete packages/shared/dist/ <main-checkout>/packages/shared/dist/`
  before running the gate.
- `implement.py` exposes no shared-resolution diagnostic today, and its
  `finish` gate cannot distinguish "shared code changed in this worktree" from
  "shared code unchanged".

## Desired change (decided)

Adopt the **worktree-local link farm** for resolution and **hard-fail** on
stale resolution:

1. Replace `_ensure_node_modules_symlink`'s whole-directory symlink with an
   idempotent link-farm creation: real `<worktree>/node_modules` containing one
   symlink per main-checkout entry, recursively for scopes (`@worklog/*`,
   `@types/*`, …), with `@worklog/shared` pointing at the worktree's
   `packages/shared` (workspace packages are resolved relative to the worktree
   via the `workspaces` field / a small allow-list). `.bin` is linked as a
   whole directory.
2. Keep the existing nested/workspace `node_modules` mirroring behaviour
   unchanged, and keep the whole step best-effort/non-fatal.
3. Add a resolution check: `@worklog/shared`'s resolved package root must equal
   `<worktree>/packages/shared`; expose it in the `start` JSON report and use
   it in `finish`.
4. In `finish`, before the test gate: if the worktree diff touches
   `packages/shared/src/**` and the check fails, hard-fail with the stale
   `<main-checkout>/packages/shared/dist` path and the remediation (re-run
   `implement.py start`/refresh from the main checkout, or run the documented
   refresh command).
5. Update the implement skill docs (worktree `node_modules` section) with the
   new model, the refresh path and the failure signature.

Rejected alternatives: automated `rsync` of the worktree's shared `dist` into
the main checkout (shared-state mutation, live `wl` contamination, concurrency
clobbering); `npm install` in the worktree (forbidden); Node resolution hooks
via `NODE_OPTIONS`/loader or tsconfig `paths` (fragile, uneven coverage across
vitest/tsx/spawned subprocesses); warning-only detection (does not satisfy
AC1).

## Key Files

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — `_ensure_node_modules_symlink` (~L1638) → link farm; `_ensure_nested_node_modules_symlinks` (~L1735) unchanged; `run_build` (~L2421)/finish gate (~L4432) → staleness hard-fail; `start` JSON report.
- `skill/implement/SKILL.md` — worktree `node_modules` contract (~L547–558): link-farm model, refresh command, failure signature, `npm install` ban.
- ContextHub `packages/shared/package.json` — `main`/`exports` → `./dist/*.js` (reference case; unchanged).
- ContextHub `packages/herdr/scripts/link-shared.mjs` — precedent for live-symlink replacement + Windows junction handling.
- ContextHub `docs/dev/implement-worktree-node-modules-verification.md` — predecessor verification doc (cross-repo reference only).
- `skill/implement/` tests — new unit tests for the link farm and the staleness helper; extend the finish-gate tests.

## Related work

- ContextHub **WL-0MVLK2JNB002E9JQ** (discovered-from; the intake that produced
  this item — deleted once this item was created, per producer decision).
- ContextHub **WL-0MVK6S4HM005GBCO** — hit the false-red symptom during the
  persist write-detection work and used the manual `rsync` workaround.
- ContextHub **WL-0MVAY631M004RZ3Q** — same defect class (stale build artefact
  behind a package resolution) for `packages/herdr`'s packaged copy; its notes
  flag this worktree-isolation gap as tracked separately.
- ContextHub **WL-0MSGQ64N2006TQB2** / **SA-0MSGS763C006SM1B** — introduced and
  verified the current `node_modules` symlink; this item supersedes that
  resolution model.
- ContextHub **WL-0MQRBT8BS00355AB** — evidence of the blast radius when the
  main checkout's `dist`/`node_modules` is mutated by tooling (why option B is
  rejected).
- **OSL-0MUFG3PJA00379CT** — nested/workspace `node_modules` symlinks; must keep
  working with the link farm.
- Prior art: ContextHub `packages/herdr/scripts/link-shared.mjs`.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk — link-farm drift.** Entries are materialised at `start`; a dependency
  added to the main checkout later is missing from a long-lived worktree.
  Mitigation: idempotent refresh, called by the resolution check, plus the
  `finish` hard-fail naming the refresh command.
- **Risk — symlink scale.** ~190 top-level entries plus scopes; creation must
  stay fast (sub-second) and must not descend into dependency trees.
- **Risk — Windows.** Directory symlinks may need privileges; use junctions as
  `link-shared.mjs` does, and keep the step non-fatal.
- **Risk — false hard-fail.** A worktree that changes `packages/shared/src/**`
  but intentionally does not rebuild would fail `finish`; the message must name
  the build/refresh command. Mitigation: `finish` builds before the gate, so
  this is only reachable when resolution itself is wrong.
- **Risk — tooling regression for other repos.** The implement skill is used by
  every project; the link farm must degrade to the old symlink behaviour when
  the repo has no workspace shared package, and the detection must no-op.
- **Assumption —** `dist/` stays gitignored in consumer checkouts, so build
  artefacts never dirty the main checkout.
- **Assumption —** agents run the sanctioned gate from the worktree root, so
  `run_tests.py`'s project-root detection targets the worktree.
- **Assumption —** POSIX is the primary platform for implement.py (Linux dev
  hosts); Windows support is best-effort via junctions.
- **Scope-creep watch:** other workspace packages could gain the same
  override; keep the mechanism generic (workspace-aware) rather than
  hard-coding `@worklog/shared`, but do not add per-package features. Any
  further isolation gaps (e.g. ContextHub `docs/dev/worktree-isolation.md`
  documentation) belong to a separate ContextHub item, not this one.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: Where should the executable fix live — SorraAgents `implement.py`, a
  ContextHub-local script + implement extension, both, or warning-only?
  **Answer (producer): "A when the SA item has been created delete this [WL]
  one"** — i.e. SorraAgents `implement.py` is the home; the originating
  ContextHub item was deleted after this SA item was created. Source:
  interactive reply in the intake session (`herdr-1792859577-1504585-28248`).
  Prior draft recommendation was (c) both; the accepted answer supersedes it.
- Q2: Which resolution mechanism — worktree-local link farm (A), automated
  `rsync` of shared `dist` into the main checkout (B), or detection +
  actionable warning only (C)? **Answer (producer): "A"** — link farm. Source:
  same reply. Rationale recorded: no shared-state mutation, per-worktree
  isolation, covers vitest/tsx/spawned subprocesses.
- Q3: Should `implement.py finish` hard-fail (not merely warn) when the
  worktree changes `packages/shared/src/**` while `@worklog/shared` still
  resolves outside the worktree? **Answer (producer): "A"** — hard-fail.
  Source: same reply. Rationale: makes false-green impossible; AC4 encodes it.
- Duplicate-work check performed (`wl search "worktree shared dist node_modules
  symlink"` in ContextHub, 15 hits reviewed; `wl search "packages/shared dist
  stale worktree build"` in SorraAgents, no hits): no duplicate. The closest
  items (WL-0MVAY631M004RZ3Q herdr packaged copy; WL-0MSGQ64N2006TQB2
  missing-`node_modules`) are completed and do not satisfy this item's ACs.
- Research (verified in the intake session): the resolution chain
  `<worktree>/node_modules -> <main>/node_modules/@worklog/shared ->
  <main>/packages/shared` and `package.json` `main`/`exports` → `./dist/*.js`;
  `implement.py` `_ensure_node_modules_symlink`, `_ensure_nested_node_modules_symlinks`,
  `run_build`, `finish`; the implement skill's "do NOT `npm install` in a
  worktree" contract; ContextHub `vitest.config.ts` worktree exclusion;
  `packages/herdr/scripts/link-shared.mjs` precedent; ContextHub
  `docs/dev/worktree-isolation.md` is missing while `AGENTS.md` links to it
  (routed to a separate ContextHub documentation item).
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **SA-0MSGS763C006SM1B** – Auto-symlink node_modules into implement worktrees (implement.py start) (completed)
- **SA-0MVEJIRZ60017H4V** – Unify test-cache namespace across worktrees and the main checkout (open)
- **SA-0MSGKAWXQ009VVG2** – Enforce git worktree usage for all implementation work (completed)

- `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` — matched: ac1, ac4, acceptance, accepted, acs (+322 more)
